summary: This lecture from Zadul-Ma'ad (Provisions for the Hereafter) by Imam Ibn al-Qayyim discusses the Prophet's dealings with the hypocrites (munafiqun) from his arrival in Medina until his death. Sheikh Ali Mashhour explains that there were approximately 12 chief hypocrites, though their influence was disproportionately large in causing discord among Muslims. The main characteristic of hypocrites is deception and lying—they profess Islam outwardly while concealing disbelief in their hearts. The Prophet was commanded to accept their outward profession while entrusting their secrets to Allah, and was forbidden to pray over them when they died. The lecture covers the various traits of hypocrites including breaking covenants, treachery, and sowing discord, as well as the two types of hypocrisy: major hypocrisy (concealing disbelief) and minor hypocrisy (exhibiting hypocritical traits while maintaining faith). The speaker emphasizes the relevance of understanding hypocrisy in modern times and stresses that fear of hypocrisy is a sign of true faith.
